summary.title: Build GIT - Learn GIT (P1)
summary.one_liner: You learn the core ideas of Git (repositories, commits, parent-linked commit history, and branches as pointers) by implementing a toy version of them in JavaScript.
takeaways: A Git repo can be modeled as an object holding commits, branches, and a HEAD reference.
Each commit stores a reference to its parent, so history is a linked list walked backwards from HEAD to produce git log.
A branch is simply a pointer to a commit; HEAD points to the current branch.
Implementing checkout means searching existing branches and either switching to one or creating a new one from the current commit.
The author uses integer ids instead of SHA-1 hashes to keep the implementation simple.
summary.summary: The author walks through building a simplified Git in JavaScript, starting with a Git repo class and a Commit class that holds an id, message, and parent. Commits are added with an incrementing integer id (noted as a simplification of Git's SHA-1 ids), and a log method traverses parent links from HEAD to return history in reverse order. The post then introduces branches as named pointers to commits, with HEAD pointing to the current branch, and adds a checkout method that switches to or creates branches. Each stage is backed by console.assert tests that mirror diagrams from git-scm.com, and the code is linked from a GitHub repo. Merging and rebasing are mentioned as the planned next part.
